text:
mia: Heads-up — on the AWQ INT8 bringup for long-prefix QA suite I see a reproducible accuracy delta when prefix-cache + continuous batching are both enabled. exact_match down ~3.2% vs fp32 baseline across 10k queries.

raj: Oof. Was that with the usual prefetch warmups?

mia: Yes same harness: prefetch enabled, kv-prefix-cache TTL default, cont-batching max latency 40ms. Config dump below. Ran on a single p4d node.

mia: ```
model: awq-gpt-13b-int8
quant: awq
prefix_cache: enabled
prefix_cache_ttl_ms: 600000
continuous_batching: enabled
cont_batch_max_latency_ms: 40
cont_batch_coalesce: true
warmup_requests: 100
eval_shard: long-prefix-qa-10k
```

sam: Can you paste the diffs vs the run where prefix-cache was off? also any sign of higher token-level perplexity or shorter output truncation?

mia: Perplexity is slightly elevated (1.04x) but not huge. Outputs are same length distribution. The failure modes look like hallucinated spans on multi-turn context; examples attached inline.

mia: Example failure: model inserts bogus factual claim after a long system prompt. On fp32 the model answers directly.

raj: Hypothesis: aggressive cont-batching coalescer might be causing KV cache interleaving/race on the awq int8 path. If a prefetched cache entry gets evicted or overwritten in the mid-request window, the attention keys could mismatch.

sam: Yeah I've seen weirdness when cont-batching groups requests with different prefix lengths and the runtime reuses KV buffers without zeroing under quantized kernels. Could be a buffer aliasing bug.

eva: Can you repro with cont-batching disabled but prefix-cache on? that isolates cont-batch as the variable. Also try cont-batching but cont_batch_coalesce=false.

mia: I did: cont-batching off + prefix-cache on = no regression. cont-batching on + prefix-cache off = no regression. Only when both on together the delta appears.

raj: Good isolation. Next: capture KV cache metrics (hits/evicts) and per-request cache_id + generation id to see if two requests share IDs. Add instrumentation: KV_CACHE_DEBUG=true and dump last 50 key hashes per worker for failing traces.

sam: Also run a micro-bakeoff with batch_size forced to 1 but cont-batching enabled (so coalescer will still try to combine). If batch_size=1 avoids it that points to coalescing logic.

mia: Will run both today. Quick note: here's the curl used to kick the eval harness so people can reproduce locally: 

mia: ```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://internal-eval.redwood/api/v1/run \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $EVAL_KEY' \
  -d '{"model":"awq-gpt-13b-int8","suite":"long-prefix-qa-10k","config":{"prefix_cache":true,"continuous_batching":true}}'
```

infra-bot: deploy:eval-harness/2026-03-19T12:34:00Z started by mia :gear:

eva: If we confirm it's a runtime coalesce bug we'll want a hotfix to zero KV buffers on allocation or pin per-request buffer ids. Also add a regression test combining quantized kernels + prefix cache + coalescer for CI.

raj: Agree. If buffer aliasing is culprit, it could also affect other quantization modes. Please include AWQ and GPTQ runs in the follow-up.

mia: Ok running the two instrumented runs now (KV debug + batch_size=1 microbakeoff). I'll paste logs and a small failing trace.

sam: Thanks—I'll review traces and look at kernel launch timeline. If it's timing-sensitive we might be able to repro with a synthetic harness that forces interleaving.

mia: quick update (logs): saw two requests with same cache_id and generation bump in the same coalesced batch; eviction count jumped by 2 right before the mismatch. Pasting redacted log excerpt: 

mia: ```
[worker-7] KV_CACHE: cache_id=0x1f4b3 gen=42 hit=0 evict=0
[worker-7] ALLOC kvbuf @0x7ffb123400 size=8192 owner=req-8912 cache_id=0x1f4b3 gen=42
[worker-7] coalesce: group_id=73 requests=[req-8912, req-8913]
[worker-7] KV_CACHE: cache_id=0x1f4b3 gen=43 hit=1 evict=1
[worker-7] REUSE kvbuf @0x7ffb123400 owner=req-8913 <-- possible alias
```

eva: That's very suggestive. Sam/raj can we triage buffer allocation codepath? probably under runtime/batching/coalesce.cc

sam: On it. I'll run a race-detector build with sanitizers on the kernel allocation paths and try to add an assert to detect reuse.

mia: Thanks all. I'll collect failing examples and open a minimal repro PR if we can isolate. Will update thread with logs + PR link. :thumbsup:
